name of our project is ASTRA -An Integrated Astronaut Health ,space risk management and mission support Platform 
Astra is an AI-powered integrated platform designed to address the challenges astronauts face during long -duration space mission. We developed a web-based prototype combining astronaut health monitoring ,space risk management, mission resource management ,and interactive astronaut training simulations. ASTRA focuses on challenges such as microgravity-related health effects, limited food and water supplies ,oxygen management ,psychological well-being ,and unexpected mission emergencies. its proposed intelligent support system aims to identify potential risk ,assist in resource planning , and provide mission based training scenarios to improve preparedness. By bringing multiple astronaut-support functions into one platform , ASTRA aims to reduce technology gaps in space mission support . Our vision is to make future human space exploration  safer   ,   smarter,more sustainable, and better prepared for mission beyond Earth.

**ASTRA 2.0: A Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer**

**What it does and how it works:** ASTRA turns Moon and Mars mission trade-offs into something students can play. Instead of memorising separate facts, a learner picks a mission (Lunar, Mars, ISS, Spacewalk or Deep Space), makes a decision under pressure, such as switching to low-power mode during a dust storm, and immediately sees how power, water, communication and safety change. Everything is connected: poor sleep raises stress, stress hurts decisions, and a 3–22 minute one-way signal delay means the crew must decide without Mission Control. Beyond the simulator, ASTRA includes a Learning Studio with animated Learn → Play → Quiz lessons (20 work offline), a 3D Lab, Health Monitor, Risk Analyzer and a Research Library linked to NASA sources. The interface is available in English, Hindi, Gujarati, Spanish and French.

**Benefits:** Students learn by doing and can fail safely. Teachers get source-backed material instead of unverified content. Offline lessons and multilingual support make it usable in low-connectivity classrooms.

**Intended impact:** To build space-health and mission-risk literacy early, and to show that astronaut decision-making is about balancing life support, radiation, power and food together. The same trade-off approach can later extend to remote healthcare, expedition and disaster-response training.

**Tools and technology:** A responsive web app hosted on Netlify, so it runs in any phone or laptop browser with no install. [Add your exact stack here, e.g. HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and any 3D or AI tools you used.]

**How it is creative:** Communication delay, food and radiation shielding are treated as gameplay mechanics, not text facts. Every module maps to published NASA research (Human Research Program, ISS bone-loss and ARED studies, Curiosity RAD radiation data, the Twins Study).

**Factors considered:** Accuracy (figures are approximate, source-linked and every simulation is labelled educational), safety and honesty (not medical advice, not real spacecraft control, not an official NASA product), accessibility (offline use, five languages, works on basic devices), and age-appropriate learning for junior astronauts.ASTRA 2.0 is a browser-based web application built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript. It runs on phones, tablets and laptops with no installation, and is deployed on Netlify so it can be shared with a single link. The interface supports five languages (English, Hindi, Gujarati, Spanish, French). The 20 Learning Studio lessons are bundled so they keep working offline, and the Mission Simulator, quizzes and concept games run on the device itself. The 3D Lab uses interactive 3D models linked to NASA source material. An optional AI assistant can answer physics, astronomy, training and risk questions when a live AI connection is configured; the app does not depend on it. No special hardware is needed.
